policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere אַתְּ and ketiv אתי are the same independent pronoun (lemma 859 b), tagged HPp2fs in both; the ketiv simply writes a final yod on the archaic form of the 2fs pronoun. ASV "Arise, I pray thee, and disguise thyself, that thou be not known to be the wife of Jeroboam" renders either identically, and no note is mapped here. The qere base stands.

Qere שִׁישַׁ֥ק and ketiv שושק are the same proper name (lemma 7895), tagged Np in both, differing in the vowel letter: yod in the qere, waw in the ketiv. As at 1KI.16.34, the difference survives transliteration — the ASV reads "Shishak king of Egypt", carrying the qere's i, where the ketiv consonants would give Shoshak (the form behind the LXX's Σουσακιμ). The name distinguishes the qere.
